exposure: Breech or other fetal position abnormalities
outcome: Postpartum urinary retention after cesarean section
cohort: The study included 2,397,168 women who underwent cesarean section, identified from the National Inpatient Sample database between 2010 and 2019.
finding: The overall incidence of postpartum urinary retention after cesarean section was 0.20%, and advanced maternal age, Asian and Pacific Islander background, comorbidities, and delivery in large or teaching hospitals were identified as significant risk factors, while low cervical CS and previous CS conferred a protective effect.
mod_finding: Low cervical cesarean section and previous cesarean section were found to be protective factors against postpartum urinary retention.
